description: Developed by Team TESSERAX, our project is a Wikipedia-style educational portal designed to make space science accessible to everyone. Featuring intuitive navigation and visual guides, it breaks down complex astronomy, planetary science, and cosmology into clear, organized topics. The platform also includes dedicated hubs for Planet X research and NASA's SPHEREx mission, making space exploration simple and engaging for all learners.
summary:
TESSERAX is an immersive, web-based digital space education platform designed to bridge the gap between complex astrophysical data and public accessibility. We developed an interactive ecosystem featuring an extensive 100+ object cosmic archive, dedicated Planet X and SPHEREx mission hubs, a context-grounded AI knowledge assistant, a live 3D global weather sphere, and universal fullscreen simulations. 

The project addresses the challenge of fragmented or overly complex scientific literature by translating dense astrophysics into a seamless, highly engaging user experience. It solves usability hurdles through multi-token smart search, drag-and-pan navigation, and real-time weather API integration. 

TESSERAX is important because it democratizes space science education, providing a high-performance, zero-cost, and visually striking resource that inspires curiosity and makes deep space exploration universally accessible to students, educators, and enthusiasts worldwide.
details:
What does TESSERAX do and how does it work?

TESSERAX (Cosmic Archives & Telemetry) is an interactive 3D space exploration, Earth observation, and astrophysics simulation web application deployed at tesssss.wasmer.app. Built as a unified digital mission control interface, it combines astronomical datasets, real-time telemetry visualizers, and physics-based simulations into seven interactive modules:

- Encyclopedia: A searchable, categorized cosmic archive covering celestial bodies, space entities, missions, constellations, comets, asteroids, and deep-space phenomena, complete with structured telemetry specs and instant 3D camera targeting.

- 3D Cosmic Map: An interactive WebGL space environment where users can orbit, zoom, and inspect planets, stars, constellations, and trajectories in three dimensions.

- Orbit Builder: A hands-on orbital mechanics sandbox allowing users to configure and test custom planetary and satellite trajectories in real time.

- SPHEREx Hub: A near-infrared spectroscopy visualizer (0.75µm – 5.0µm) that simulates emission and absorption spectral bands across celestial objects to identify chemical signatures such as H2O, CO2, CH4, and silicates.

- Planet X Sim & Earth Telemetry: A planetary observation module featuring satellite and thermal view modes, atmospheric weather overlays, and space-to-Earth impact simulations (such as eclipse alignments and geomagnetic solar storms).

- Star Forge (Stellar Collapse): A stellar physics survival simulation where players balance nuclear fusion pressure against gravitational collapse across four stellar stages—Red Dwarf, Yellow Dwarf, Blue Giant, and Hypergiant—to prevent catastrophic black hole formation.

- Trivia & Facts: An interactive space knowledge module designed to test and reinforce concepts in astronomy, planetary science, and space exploration.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

Astrophysics, near-infrared spectroscopy, and orbital mechanics are often locked behind complex raw datasets or static textbooks that can feel intimidating to students and the general public. TESSERAX bridges this gap by turning NASA and geospatial science concepts into tactile, interactive 3D simulations. Its intended impact is to democratize space science education, spark STEM curiosity, and help learners visually understand how stellar evolution, spectral analysis, and cosmic events operate and affect Earth.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use?

- Frontend & 3D Graphics: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js / WebGL, custom GLSL shaders (for planetary atmospheres, thermal heatmaps, and stellar plasma), and HTML5 Canvas 2D (for real-time spectrograph rendering).

- Data & Geospatial APIs: NASA Open APIs (NeoWs Near-Earth Object Web Service, DONKI Space Weather Database, NASA Exoplanet Archive), Google Maps Platform (3D Earth Tiles and Weather Telemetry), and structured offline fallback JSON datasets.

- Hosting & Development Environment: Hosted live on Wasmer (tesssss.wasmer.app) and developed on standard multi-core workstations using modern web browsers and developer tools.

How is our project creative and what factors did our team consider?

Rather than creating a passive encyclopedia or a single-purpose chart, we designed TESSERAX as an integrated cosmic workspace where data exploration, sandbox building (Orbit Builder), and physics gameplay (Star Forge) reinforce one another. Our team prioritized:

- Performance & Reliability: Ensuring smooth 3D rendering and clean, responsive navigation across devices, supported by local fallback datasets so simulations remain fast and functional even under limited network conditions.

- Scientific Clarity: Translating abstract principles—such as stellar fusion equilibrium, near-infrared absorption dips, and orbital dynamics—into intuitive visual controls.

- Compliance & Originality: Building original UI layouts, custom shaders, and educational tools that present public scientific knowledge clearly without misusing official NASA logos or agency branding.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

During the development of TESSERAX (tesssss.wasmer.app), our team utilized Super Intelligence (SI) tools—specifically ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and the Freebuff tool (along with their underlying large language and generative models)—to accelerate software development, data formatting, and UI prototyping. In strict compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, no NASA logos, flags, or official mission identifiers were generated, modified, or embedded via SI tools, and all SI-assisted elements are disclosed below:

- Code & Software Architecture (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini): SI coding assistants were used to help structure Three.js 3D rendering scenes, write custom GLSL shader logic, refine CSS flexbox navigation alignment, and debug interactive simulation loops for modules including Star Forge, Orbit Builder, and the SPHEREx Hub spectrograph. All generated code was reviewed, adapted, and integrated by our team.

- Scientific Data Structuring & Copywriting (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini): SI models assisted in organizing structured JSON encyclopedia entries (covering celestial bodies, space missions, constellations, and phenomena), generating Trivia & Facts questions, and editing clear educational descriptions across the user interface.

- Visual & Asset Prototyping (Freebuff Tool): The Freebuff tool was used during early visual ideation and UI asset prototyping. Any SI-assisted visual assets included in the project carry clear descriptive metadata and visible indicators acknowledging their SI-generated origin.

- Audio: No pre-recorded SI-generated audio files are included in the final submission; any browser-synthesized Web Audio API sound effects are documented in the application metadata.
